STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: One criterion fails under reproduction: a 304 drops a handler-set `Last-Modified`, but criterion 4 says the 304 keeps other headers. Everything else I threw at it held: wire HEAD, Flush streaming, Unwrap via ResponseController, sniffing, compression, 1xx, panics, and a 20,000-case If-None-Match differential against `http.ServeContent`. The probe files are deleted and `git status` matches the start.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probes were written under `middleware/zz_probe*_etag_test.go` and deleted; `git status` shows only the original `M README.md`, `A middleware/etag.go`, `A middleware/etag_test.go`)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] `Last-Modified` is deleted on 304 (etag.go `h.Del("Last-Modified")`). Criterion 4 says the 304 keeps other headers and drops only Content-Type, Content-Length and Content-Encoding. Reproduced with a real server: handler sets `Last-Modified`, request has `If-None-Match: *`, 304 arrives with `Last-Modified=""`. Note that Go's `writeNotModified` does the same when an ETag is present, so this is parity with net/http, but it contradicts the criterion's literal list. The orchestrator must decide whether to keep the criterion or the parity.
- [minor] Panic after buffered writes under `ETag` outer and `Recoverer` inner yields 200 with the partial body and a computed ETag. Not reproduced as a regression: a plain net/http baseline gives the same 200 "partial", so this is not caused by the diff.
- [minor] Handler setting `ETag` to `""` gets a computed tag instead of an empty one. Behaviour is reasonable, but the criterion's "handler did not set an ETag" is ambiguous here. Not reproduced as a failure.

CHECKS:
- `go test` probe, real server: HEAD 304 with `W/` request tag → pass
- Wire HEAD Content-Length vs plain net/http (both 5) → pass
- Flush over real connection: "first" arrives while handler is blocked, status 200, body "second", no ETag → pass
- `http.NewResponseController` SetWriteDeadline / SetReadDeadline through Unwrap → pass (nil errors)
- Content-Type sniffing for chunked writes vs plain net/http → pass (text/html, same)
- Differential If-None-Match vs `http.ServeContent`, 20,000 random single-line lists (quoted/weak/unquoted/unterminated/stray commas/whitespace/`W/W/`) → pass, zero mismatches (`*` excluded, as the accepted deviation)
- 103 then 200 on the wire with `If-None-Match: *` → final 304, 103 delivered → pass (recorder-based 103 probe was a recorder artifact, not a bug)
- Gzip via `Compress` inside `ETag`, body intact, 304 on re-request → pass
- Two `If-None-Match` lines, first empty, second matching → 304 → pass
- `WriteHeader(404)` then `Flush` with HEAD and `*` → 404, no ETag → pass
- `WriteHeader(0)` panics with `invalid WriteHeader code 0`, same as net/http → pass
- Concurrent 32 wire requests through the router under `-race` → pass
- Existing `Hijack`/`Push` error wording matches compress.go's `chi/middleware: ...` form → pass (by inspection)

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should the 304 keep `Last-Modified` (criterion 4 literal) or drop it (current code, matches net/http's `writeNotModified`)? The orchestrator must choose and align the test `TestETagNotModifiedHeaders`, which currently asserts the deletion.
